title: Ola Electric Narrows Q1 Loss as EV Sales Rebound After Reset Year
excerpt: The Bhavish Aggarwal-led company posted a net loss of ₹336 crore for the June quarter, down from ₹428 crore a year earlier, as higher scooter sales and cost cuts offset a tough commodity environment.
body:
• Ola Electric's net loss narrowed 21% to ₹336 crore ($35.3 million) in Q1 FY27 from ₹428 crore a year earlier, driven by higher sales and lower operating expenses
  • The results follow a brutal FY26 in which revenue nearly halved to ₹2,253 crore and deliveries dropped to 1.74 lakh units from 3.08 lakh
  • Management had guided for 40,000-45,000 orders and revenue of ₹500-550 crore in Q1 FY27, roughly double the March quarter
  • The stock has fallen about 75% from its post-listing peak of ₹157.53, trading near ₹37-38 heading into the results

Ola Electric Mobility reported a narrower first-quarter loss on Friday, offering early evidence that the Indian electric two-wheeler maker's volume recovery is translating into improved financials after a year the company itself described as a "reset."

The Bhavish Aggarwal-led company posted a consolidated net loss of ₹336 crore ($35.3 million) for the quarter ended June 2026, compared with a loss of ₹428 crore in the same period last year, according to Reuters. Higher electric scooter sales and lower operating expenses helped offset a challenging commodity environment marked by elevated raw material costs.

The Reset Year That Preceded the Rebound

The Q1 FY27 improvement follows what was arguably the most difficult year in Ola Electric's short history as a public company. Full-year FY26 revenue fell to ₹2,253 crore from ₹4,514 crore in FY25, while deliveries collapsed from 3,07,846 units to just 1,73,794. The top line shrank every quarter — from ₹828 crore in Q1 FY26 to ₹690 crore in Q2, ₹470 crore in Q3, and just ₹265 crore by Q4.

Management used the downturn to restructure operations, stabilize after-sales service, cut costs, and push gross margins higher. By Q4 FY26, consolidated gross margins had climbed to 38.5%, up from 13.7% a year earlier, and the company posted its first operating cash-flow positive quarter.

"Q4 was lower revenue because it was also a quarter where we focused a lot on our operations, to fix the operations, and then scale again."

— Bhavish Aggarwal, Founder and CMD, Ola Electric

Volume Recovery Takes Shape

Heading into Q1 FY27, Ola Electric guided for 40,000-45,000 orders and consolidated revenue of ₹500-550 crore, roughly double the ₹265 crore posted in Q4 FY26. VAHAN registration data had shown momentum building: registrations climbed from about 10,000 units in March to 12,000 in April and were trending toward 14,000-15,000 in May.

By mid-May, Q1 FY27 registrations on the VAHAN portal had already surpassed the entire Q4 FY26 tally of 22,221 units with weeks remaining in the quarter. Aggarwal said order growth was running ahead of registrations, and inventory days had fallen to just three to four days.

Operating expenses also came down sharply during FY26. Total opex including leases fell to ₹428 crore in Q4 FY26 from ₹844 crore a year earlier, and management guided for monthly operating expenses to fall further to ₹100-120 crore as utilization improved.

Competition Remains Fierce

Ola Electric faces an intensifying battle in India's electric two-wheeler market. Rivals Bajaj Auto, TVS Motor, and Ather Energy have gained share, and the broader market declined more than 22% in April even as Ola's registrations grew. In Q1 FY26, Ola delivered 68,192 scooters, down from 1,25,198 a year earlier, underscoring the ground lost to competitors.

The company's in-house technology push is central to its margin strategy. Ola's Gigafactory has been commissioned at 2.5 GWh capacity with plans to reach 5.9 GWh by March 2026. Its proprietary 4680 Bharat Cell began powering vehicles starting Navratri, and the company has developed heavy rare earth-free motors for deployment from Q3 FY26 onward.

What Investors Are Watching

With the stock down roughly 75% from its all-time high, the Q1 FY27 results are a critical test of whether Ola Electric can deliver the turnaround Aggarwal has been promising. The company has said consolidated adjusted operating EBITDA breakeven is achievable at monthly sales volumes of 20,000-25,000 units, and it expects the current rebound to push monthly volumes to 17,000-18,000 units, with better service and inventory management potentially lifting that to 20,000-22,000.

Detailed financials, including revenue, margins, and delivery figures for Q1 FY27, are expected in the company's full earnings release. For now, the narrower loss suggests the reset year was not wasted — but proving it was worthwhile will require sustained execution in the quarters ahead.
nri_angle: Ola Electric, one of India's most closely watched EV startups, shows early signs of a turnaround after a bruising reset year that sent its stock down 75%.
